frasi_scheda.budget: The scheme is in its fifth year, with a budget of £400 million for 2026/27.
frasi_scheda.pagato: Across the first four years of the scheme, over £560 million was paid out through grants.
frasi_scheda.fino: The Government confirmed funding for further years up to 2029/30 through the Warm Homes Plan in January 2026.
frasi_scheda.aprile2026: 28 April 2026: Expansion of eligibility for multi-technology installations; the introduction of £2,500 grants for AAHPs; relaxing the requirement for a valid EPC; mandating that installers deduct the BUS grants from upfront costs; mandating the Microgeneration Certification Scheme (MCS) as the sole certification scheme. Statistics on the uptake of AAHPs will be incorporated into this release once the first grants have been paid.
frasi_scheda.luglio2026: 21 July 2026: Installers could apply on behalf of eligible off-gas grid property owners in England and Wales for a £9,000 grant to support the installation of an air-to-water or ground source heat pump. This grant was available for off-gas grid properties heated by oil or liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).
frasi_scheda.ottobre2023: 23 October 2023: Increase in grant levels for heat pump technologies from £5,000 for air-to-water heat pumps and £6,000 for ground source heat pumps to £7,500 for both.
frasi_scheda.maggio2024: 8 May 2024: Removal of the requirement to have no outstanding recommendations for loft and cavity wall insulation on the property’s Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) certificate.
frasi_scheda.voucher_validi: AWHP, AAHP and biomass boiler vouchers are valid for 3 months while GSHP vouchers are valid for 6 months.
frasi_scheda.primo_arrivato: Vouchers are issued on a first come, first served basis, to applicants who meet the eligibility requirements until the budget cap for the financial year is reached.
frasi_scheda.prezzo_pagato: The price paid by the property owner is the total cost of the installation less the value of the grant.

commento: a) Up until the end of September 2026, there were 160,874 BUS voucher applications received. The majority of these were for grants towards AWHP installations (98%). [Table 1.1]

b) The total number of applications in September 2026 across all technology types (9,738) was 30% higher than the previous month (August 2026: 7,486). September 2026 was the highest number of voucher applications in a month since the scheme started and is 138% higher than the same month of the previous year (September 2025; 4,089). [Table M1.1]. From July 2026, installers could apply on behalf of owners of eligible off-gas-grid properties heated by LPG or oil for a £9,000 grant towards installing an air-to-water or ground source heat pump (see Scheme background for details).From this scheme change until the end of September, 8,107 applications for the £9,000 grant were received. These applications were 32% of the 25,374 total applications received in July to September 2026.

c) Up until the end of September 2026 a total of 131,619 vouchers were issued. September 2026 volumes (6,298) were 7% higher than the previous month (August 2026; 5,903) and 73% higher than the same month in the previous year (September 2025; 3,640). [Table M1.1]. September 2026 was the highest number of vouchers issued in a month since the scheme started. In September 2026, 2,035 vouchers issued were for the £9,000 grant, representing 32% of all vouchers issued in the month.

d) The number of redemption applications in September 2026 across all technology types (3,972) was 19% higher than the previous month (August 2026; 3,329). [Table M1.1]. September 2026 was the highest number of redemption applications in a month since the scheme started. In September 2026, 1,446 redemption applications were for the £9,000 grant, representing 36% of total redemption applications received in the month.

e) There were 3,332 redemptions paid in September 2026, bringing the total number of redemptions paid through the scheme to 96,611. [Table M1.1]. September 2026 was the highest number of redemptions paid in a month since the scheme started. In September 2026, 1,205 redemptions paid were for the £9,000 grant, representing 36% of total redemptions paid in the month.

f) To the end of September 2026, the national and regional breakdown for redemptions paid continued to be broadly similar to previous months. Of the total number of redemptions paid, the largest number were for installations at properties in the South East region (19,069; 20%), followed by the South West region (17,168; 18%). The fewest number of redemptions paid were in the North East region (3,033; 3%). Wales accounted for 5% of the total (5,148 redemptions paid). [Table 1.2A]

g) Of the total 96,611 installations with BUS redemptions paid up to the end of September 2026, the largest proportion (55%) replaced gas systems, followed by oil (18%) and then properties which did not previously have a heating system at all (13%). [Table 1.3]

h) The nominal median cost of an AWHP and GSHP in the most recent quarter (2026 Q3; July to September) was £12,826 and £34,630, respectively (including the grant value). After adjusting for inflation, the median cost of an AWHP in 2026 Q3 is 14% lower than the same period in the first year of the scheme (2022 Q3; £14,989). The underlying mix of heat pump sizes can influence the trend in median costs over time. [Table Q1.1A and Q1.1B]

i) Of all redemptions paid on the scheme to the end of September 2026, there has been an almost even split between installations in urban and rural areas, 51% urban to 49% rural. The majority of properties in receipt of grants were on the gas grid (59,162; 61%). [Tables 1.5 and 1.6]
